title: adaptive-drain-scheduler-for-progressive-dedicated-pool-rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Dedicated GPU pools require safe upgrade mechanisms that avoid simultaneous capacity drops and SLO regressions. Existing wave-based drains are too coarse for mixed-tenant pools and don't react to real-time load/queue changes. Goal: implement an Adaptive Drain Scheduler (ADS) that slices a GPU pool into small, telemetry-driven cohorts and coordinates with the autoscaler and routing layer to perform progressive drains with automatic fallback and rollback triggers. The ADS should support LTS-channel-aware gating, canary slices, and operator pause/resume.

Scope: controller + operator CLI + guardrail hooks in autoscaler. Not in scope: hardware firmware upgrades and on-prem air-gapped upgrade flows (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: No more than 5% of overall provisioned GPU vRAM capacity removed concurrently during normal upgrades (measured across sample fleets)
No increase above 5% in p99 inference latency during staged rollouts under baseline load profile in staging clusters
Automatic rollback triggers if error rate or latency breach sustained for >2m for a slice
Supports LTS channel pinning: ability to choose rollout path (canary -> ramp -> full) per LTS channel
Operator can pause/resume/skip slices from the Console and via CLI
Observability: rollout dashboard shows per-slice telemetry (errors/latency/capacity delta) and a single-click abort that drains back to previous version
design_notes: ADS uses three core concepts: slice (subset of nodes by label/affinity), window (timebox for draining/evacuation), and headroom budget (autoscaler-backed capacity allowance). The controller obtains a dynamic headroom budget from the autoscaler API and gates starting a slice drain until the budget is available. Slice size is adaptive: base slice = 3 nodes or 10% of pool (whichever smaller) and will shrink when cluster queue depth or tail-latency rises. Each slice rollout runs a canary (1 node) for traffic-shifted health checks and synthetic probe traffic for model correctness. LTS-aware gating: rollout plans are associated with LTS tags so we can enforce different ramp rates for LTS vs non-LTS images. Operators can annotate nodes for priority and pin critical workers to skip drains.
implementation_notes: Components: 1) ads-controller (K8s-style operator) that schedules slice state machine, 2) autoscaler protocol shim to request headroom and pre-warm instances, 3) routing-hook that can redirect new requests away from draining nodes, 4) metrics exporter and rollout dashboard integration. State machine states: Pending -> Prewarm -> Cordon -> Drain -> Validate -> Promote -> Cleanup or Rollback. Interactions: cordon triggers the runtime to stop new sessions; drain ensures KV cache persistence where required and triggers graceful session migration. Use leader-elected controller with optimistic concurrency and retries. Persist rollout metadata in ConfigMap/CRD and Mirror to Console audit logs. All control-plane RPCs must be idempotent. Implementation will reuse existing drain libraries but add slice bucketing and autoscaler handshakes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller logic + state transitions. Integration tests in staging: synthetic workload (mix of long KV-backed sessions and short prompts) and autoscaler load tests. Chaos tests: simulate node termination during Prewarm and during Drain to ensure rollback path intact. Load-sustained tests: run a 48-hour soak in staging with rolling upgrades at 2% per hour and validate latency and error budgets. Smoke tests to validate LTS gating and pause/resume via Console. Add e2e: canary should detect model output regressions using existing evaluation harness and trigger abort. Test metrics tracked in dashboard: fail rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue length, headroom provision time.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flag behind runtime-1.20. 2) Unit + integration green. 3) Deploy ads-controller to internal staging fleet; run a single canary slice on a low-traffic pool. 4) Run progressive ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30-minute observation windows; adjust per telemetry. 5) On success, enable for non-critical dedicated pools. 6) Schedule LTS channel runs with more conservative ramps (1% -> 3% -> 10% -> 100%). 7) Post-rollout audit and metrics review after 72 hours. Rollback: controller issues promote-backflow to reattach traffic and triggers autoscaler to provision nodes matching prior version.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Autoscaler provisioning lag causes slices to fail or prolonged SLO breach. Mitigation: require prewarm handshake and configurable max wait timeout; if headroom not met, pause rollout and alert on-call.

Risk: KV cache loss during node migration leads to higher tail latency. Mitigation: KV-aware drain step with background cache copy and temporary sticky routing for ongoing sessions until eviction threshold reached.

Risk: Controller bug causes repeated rollbacks and thrash. Mitigation: rollout rate-limiter, backoff between retries, and circuit-breaker to halt after 3 failed slices with operator intervention required.
Risk: Operator error misconfigures slice size. Mitigation: safe defaults and Console warnings; require explicit confirmation for >20% slice sizes.

Risk: LTS gating complexity causes divergence across fleets. Mitigation: enforce LTS policy via server-side validation and add a dry-run mode that simulates the rollout on metadata only before applying.

2026-02-18 - Marisol Gomez (runtime): Left design feedback — suggested adding KV-awareness to drain step and tightening canary validation windows. Will follow up with a small sketch of cache-copy flow.
2026-02-22 - Liam Chen: POC for controller events merged to feature branch. PR #5821 opened. Noted autoscaler API gap: needs a prewarm endpoint (filed ENG-27131).
2026-03-03 - Carlos Ruiz (SRE): Runbook draft attached to Confluence. SRE requested alerting for headroom wait >5m and automatic pause when more than 2 slices in retry state.
2026-03-08 - Design review: Approved with minor changes. Action item: add circuit-breaker and operator confirmation for large slices (ENG-27138).

2026-03-12 - Liam Chen: Integration tests in staging passed for 1% and 5% ramps. Observed a 2.7% p99 increase under a synthetic long-tail workload; reduced base slice from 3 nodes to 2 for small pools. Next: schedule canary on dedicated-north-2 pool.
